sculpture.name: Figure
sculpture.title: Lizard Man Figure (Moko)
sculpture.reason: This is a classic Rapa Nui moko miro (lizard-man figure), a known carved wood genre from Easter Island with inlaid obsidian/bone eyes, matching the claimed ethnicity and the museum's attribution.

sculpture.name: skulptur, sten, fotografi, photograph
sculpture.title: skulptur, sten, fotografi, photograph
sculpture.reason: The photo documents small stone carvings (moai-style heads/figures and a pestle-like object) collected on Rapa Nui/Easter Island during the Vanadis expedition, matching the claimed Rapa Nui origin; it is a museum documentary photo of actual stone sculptures used/made by the Rapa Nui people.

sculpture.name: Figure
sculpture.title: Male Figure (Moai Kavakava)
sculpture.reason: A classic Rapa Nui moai kavakava figure—emaciated carved wooden ancestor figure with prominent ribs, goatee, and inlaid obsidian/bone eyes—a well-known Rapa Nui sculptural form.

sculpture.name: Figure
sculpture.title: Male Figure (Moai Tangata)
sculpture.reason: This is a classic Moai Tangata ata, a carved wooden standing male figure with inlaid obsidian/bone eyes and ribs visible, a well-known Rapa Nui sculptural tradition carved by the islanders themselves.

sculpture.name: Figure
sculpture.title: Moko (lizardman figure)
sculpture.reason: This is a classic Rapa Nui moko miro (lizard-man figure), a carved wooden pendant with obsidian and bone inlaid eyes, a well-documented traditional Rapa Nui art form worn by men as ornament.

sculpture.name: Figure
sculpture.title: Moai papa (female figure)
sculpture.reason: This is a classic moai papa (wooden female figure) with carved ribs, incised details, and obsidian/bone inlaid eyes, a well-documented Rapa Nui sculptural type carved in wood for ceremonial purposes.

household.name: Paddle
household.title: Rapa (dance paddle)
household.reason: This shows a wooden rapa (dance paddle) with a carved anthropomorphic head at the top, a classic Rapa Nui ceremonial dance implement used in traditional performance.

household.name: fotografi, photograph
household.title: fotografi, photograph
household.reason: A museum studio photo of a set of carved wooden paddles/clubs with carved head finials (ao, rapa, and ua-type staffs), documented as collected on Easter Island during the Vanadis voyage of 1883-85 — these are classic Rapa Nui carved wooden implements.

household.name: Dance paddle
household.title: Dance Paddle (Rapa)
household.reason: This is a classic Rapa Nui carved wooden Rapa dance paddle, with the characteristic two-faced ovoid head and elongated handle—an object distinctive of Rapa Nui material culture.

household.name: objects, plait bag, bag, photograph, ph
household.title: objects, plait bag, bag, photograph, ph
household.reason: The image shows a plaited bag made from Scirpus (sedge) fiber, documented as from Rapa Nui (Easter Island) and collected there, a plausible traditional craft object of the Rapa Nui people despite being labeled "photo."

jewelry.name: Gorget
jewelry.title: Rei miro (gorget)
jewelry.reason: This is a rei miro, a crescent-shaped wooden breast ornament carved with Janus-faced heads, a well-documented Rapa Nui prestige object worn by chiefs. It is a body ornament, not a weapon, so the claimed "arms" category is wrong, but it is correctly attributed to the Rapa Nui.

architectural.name: fotografi, photograph
architectural.title: fotografi, photograph
architectural.reason: Photograph from Carl Skottsberg's 1916–17 expedition showing a traditional Rapa Nui dry-stone house ("hare moa" or similar stone structure) on Easter Island, a documentary image of a built structure made by the islanders.

architectural.name: fotografi, photograph
architectural.title: fotografi, photograph
architectural.reason: The photo shows a traditional stone house (hare moa / stone chicken house or similar dry-stone structure) on Rapa Nui, photographed during the 1916–17 Swedish expedition, with a person seated at its entrance; this is a documentary photo of Rapa Nui vernacular architecture.
